blk_part_01_part_1_moon_viewing_in_japan.text: To see how people spend time in autumn in Japan, start with Tsukimi, the Japanese autumn moon-viewing custom. Jugoya is the fifteenth night of the eighth lunar month. In 2026, Tsukimi is on 25 September. People display dango, round rice dumplings, and susuki, or silver grass. The round dango stand for the full moon. The grass stands for rice and good crops.

blk_part_05_part_5_welcoming_the_dead_in.text: Families make an ofrenda, a home offering or shrine for the dead. They place favourite dishes, flowers, candles, and handmade objects around home shrines and tombs. Flower petals and candles can also mark paths. The period comes at the end of the yearly maize, or corn, growing cycle. UNESCO put this living tradition on its Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2008.
